Patient journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

01

Find and enquire

Patients and families compare doctors, services, check-up packages, prices and insurance acceptance, often by WhatsApp or phone and often late in the evening.

Touchpoints

  • Website and Google Business Profile
  • WhatsApp and phone enquiries
  • Referring doctor's advice
  • Health check-up and test price pages

Accountable owner

Patient relations or contact center lead

Automations on this stage

Find and enquire · 3–4 weeks

Safe enquiry routing for clinics and labs

Incoming WhatsApp and website messages are sorted by intent. Fees, timings, check-up packages, test preparation and directions are answered from approved content; symptoms, result questions and complaints go to the right staff member, and emergencies get an immediate instruction.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Book and prepare

The patient books a consultation, a home collection window or a prescription order, and receives preparation instructions such as fasting or documents to bring.

Touchpoints

  • Appointment booking
  • Home sample collection booking
  • Prescription upload and order
  • Pre-visit instructions

Accountable owner

Front-office manager or pharmacist in charge

Automations on this stage

Book and prepare · 4–6 weeks

WhatsApp appointment booking, reminders and rescheduling

Patients book consultations and health check-ups on WhatsApp against live HIS or EMR slots, receive approved reminders with preparation notes, and confirm, reschedule or cancel in one tap. Released slots go back to the diary and to the waitlist.

View the blueprint ↗Book and prepare · 4–6 weeks

Home sample collection scheduling and phlebotomist routing

Collection requests from WhatsApp, the website or the call center are checked for serviceable pincodes, booked into slots, batched into phlebotomist routes and tracked through to barcode handover at the lab.

View the blueprint ↗Book and prepare · 5–7 weeks

Prescription order intake with pharmacist verification

Orders from the pharmacy's app, website or counter scan land in one verification queue. AI extracts medicine lines from the prescription image as a draft, and a registered pharmacist checks every line against the original before anything is billed or dispensed.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Arrive and register

Registration, ABHA Scan and Share where the facility participates, token issue, waiting and consultation. For many patients this is where the experience is won or lost.

Touchpoints

  • Registration desk or QR self-registration
  • OPD token and waiting area
  • Consulting room call
  • Billing counter

Accountable owner

OPD operations manager

Automations on this stage

Arrive and register · 4–5 weeks

OPD pre-registration, ABHA Scan and Share and token updates

Patients pre-register before they arrive, can use ABHA Scan and Share where the facility participates, and receive their token and queue position on WhatsApp, so they can wait outside a crowded hall and return when called.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Treatment and admission

Day-care procedures, recurring sessions, admissions and inpatient stays, with bed allocation, insurance authorization and coordination across nursing, billing and housekeeping.

Touchpoints

  • Admission desk
  • TPA and insurance desk
  • Wards and nursing stations
  • Day-care, dialysis and chemotherapy units

Accountable owner

Nursing superintendent and admissions head

Automations on this stage

Treatment and admission · 2–4 weeks

Recurring session scheduling for dialysis, chemo and physiotherapy

Treatment plans with repeating sessions become scheduled series with chair or machine capacity checked, reminders sent before each session, and missed sessions flagged to the nurse in charge the same day.

View the blueprint ↗Treatment and admission · 6–8 weeks

Cashless pre-authorization document tracker

Each insured admission or day-care procedure gets a live checklist of the documents its insurer or TPA needs, secure upload links for the family, timers on insurer queries and an alert when discharge authorization is waiting.

View the blueprint ↗Treatment and admission · 5–7 weeks

Bed availability, admission and shift-coverage alerts

Admission requests, discharge orders, housekeeping turnaround and shift gaps flow into one internal channel with clear owners, so bed managers and nursing in-charges act on the same live picture instead of phone relays.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Results and reports

Pathologists and radiologists authorize reports, which reach the patient and, with consent, the referring doctor. Critical values are escalated to the responsible clinician first.

Touchpoints

  • LIS and RIS report authorization
  • Report-ready notification
  • Critical value call
  • Referring doctor copy

Accountable owner

Lab director or lab quality manager

Automations on this stage

Results and reports · 4–6 weeks

Consented lab and radiology report delivery

Once a pathologist or radiologist authorizes a report, the patient receives a notification with a secure, expiring link, and the referring doctor gets a copy only where the patient agreed. Reports are linked to ABHA where the lab participates in ABDM.

View the blueprint ↗Results and reports · 3–5 weeks

Critical result escalation with recorded read-back

When the LIS flags a result outside the lab's approved critical limits, the on-duty pathologist is paged at once, phones the responsible clinician and records the read-back. Unacknowledged alerts climb an agreed escalation ladder.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Discharge and continuing care

Discharge summaries, follow-up visits, check-ins and medicine refills that keep recovery and chronic care on track after the patient leaves.

Touchpoints

  • Discharge summary handover
  • Post-discharge check-in
  • Follow-up appointment
  • Refill reminder

Accountable owner

Care coordination lead or pharmacist in charge

Automations on this stage

Discharge and continuing care · 4–6 weeks

Discharge summary sharing and post-discharge follow-up

When the consultant signs the discharge summary, the patient receives a secure link, follow-up reminders and structured check-ins on the days the care team chose. Any reported concern goes to a care coordinator nurse, never to an automated reply.

View the blueprint ↗Discharge and continuing care · 3–5 weeks

Refill-due reminders with pharmacist checks

Chronic patients who opt in receive a reminder when a refill may be due, calculated from the quantity and directions the pharmacist recorded. Every reorder still needs a valid prescription and a pharmacist's verification.

View the blueprint ↗
07

Feedback and relationships

Patients rate their experience, complaints are recovered and recorded, and relationships with referring doctors are reviewed on service quality rather than incentives.

Touchpoints

  • Feedback request
  • Grievance and call-back
  • Referring doctor service review
  • Public reviews

Accountable owner

Quality and patient experience manager

Automations on this stage

Feedback and relationships · 2–4 weeks

Patient feedback and service recovery

A short feedback request follows each visit, discharge, report or pharmacy order. Low scores and complaints open tickets with owners and deadlines, possible clinical concerns go to the quality team, and themes are reviewed every week.

View the blueprint ↗Feedback and relationships · 3–4 weeks

Referring-doctor relationship CRM

Each referring doctor and clinic gets a CRM record of report preferences, turnaround issues, open tickets and service reviews, so relationship managers fix problems early. The CRM has no fields for referral payments, which medical ethics rules prohibit.

View the blueprint ↗

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Safe enquiry routing for clinics and labsFind and enquireThe clinic nurse or the lab's medical officer answers every symptom, medicine or result question; front-office staff take complaints and anything the model is unsure about. The clinical lead approves the emergency word list and the FAQ before go-live.
WhatsApp appointment booking, reminders and reschedulingBook and prepareFront-office staff handle anything outside the booking rules, such as priority appointments or patients who reply with symptoms, which go to the duty nurse. The OPD coordinator approves every delay or cancellation message before it is sent.
Home sample collection scheduling and phlebotomist routingBook and prepareThe collection coordinator confirms every test list against the prescription and resolves special preparation questions with the lab's medical officer. The phlebotomist verifies the patient's identity on site before collecting.
Prescription order intake with pharmacist verificationBook and prepareA registered pharmacist verifies every prescription and every line before billing or dispensing, and decides when the original prescription must be seen at pickup or delivery. Schedule X items need the original prescription at the counter and are never confirmed remotely.
OPD pre-registration, ABHA Scan and Share and token updatesArrive and registerThe OPD coordinator approves delay notices and decides on out-of-turn priority for elderly, pregnant or visibly unwell patients. Triage nurses, not the system, decide clinical priority.
Recurring session scheduling for dialysis, chemo and physiotherapyTreatment and admissionThe unit coordinator approves schedule changes. The nurse in charge follows up every missed session and escalates to the treating doctor, who alone decides any change to the treatment plan.
Cashless pre-authorization document trackerTreatment and admissionThe TPA desk executive checks every extracted field and submits the request; the treating doctor writes and signs the clinical justification and answers medical queries. No document goes to an insurer automatically.
Bed availability, admission and shift-coverage alertsTreatment and admissionThe bed manager allocates beds and doctors decide clinical priority between waiting patients. The nursing in-charge approves every swap and decides how to cover a gap. Alerts inform these people; they never assign beds or staff on their own.
Consented lab and radiology report deliveryResults and reportsOnly reports authorized by a pathologist or radiologist are released, and the automation never explains results. Questions about a result go to the lab's medical staff or the referring doctor, and critical values follow the escalation path before any notification.
Critical result escalation with recorded read-backResults and reportsA pathologist or senior technologist verifies every critical result and speaks personally to the clinician, or to the patient when there is no referring clinician. The automation never puts critical values in messages or interprets them; it pages people and keeps the record.
Discharge summary sharing and post-discharge follow-upDischarge and continuing careA care coordinator nurse reviews every flagged reply and calls the patient, and the treating doctor decides any change to medicines or care. AI only summarizes free-text replies for the nurse and never advises the patient.
Refill-due reminders with pharmacist checksDischarge and continuing careThe pharmacist verifies the prescription for every reorder and can pause reminders for any customer. Nothing is dispensed on the strength of a reminder, and dose questions go to the pharmacist or the prescribing doctor.
Patient feedback and service recoveryFeedback and relationshipsPatient relations staff or the store manager call every low-score patient, and the quality team or medical superintendent reviews any comment that may describe a clinical problem. Model theme labels are checked during the weekly review.
Referring-doctor relationship CRMFeedback and relationshipsThe relationship manager owns each doctor record and decides on follow-up, and the lab director reviews the monthly summaries. Commercial terms with hospitals and institutions are handled by management outside the automation, under the lab's ethics policy.
